ges.metaDesc: Turnkey solar from survey to commissioning: zoning and permits, project development, EPC and operations under one roof.
ges.title: Solar Power Plants
ges.intro: From rooftops to open fields, farmland to car parks — we design your plant, run its permits, build and operate it. Zoning, EIA and licensing included, end to end.

rooftop.title: Rooftop PV
rooftop.desc: A solar plant built on a building's roof; homes, businesses, factories and warehouses all qualify. The electricity feeds the building's own consumption first, and any surplus is exported to the grid. We run every step, from permits through installation, commissioning and the operations period.
rooftop.alt: Aerial view of a factory roof covered in solar panels

ground.title: Ground-Mount PV
ground.desc: A solar plant built on open land; the panel layout follows the terrain's slope and orientation. The electricity reaches the grid over a transmission line and is net-metered or sold. We manage EIA and zoning permits plus the grid-connection process end to end; installation and operations included.
ground.alt: Aerial view of ground-mounted solar array rows on open land

agripv.title: Agri-PV
agripv.desc: A solar plant built primarily for agricultural irrigation. Planting and farm machinery still pass beneath the panels; the same parcel yields both crops and electricity.
agripv.alt: A cow grazing in front of a solar array on farmland

carport.title: Carport PV
carport.desc: A plant whose panels sit on a steel canopy sheltering the cars beneath. It provides shade and generates electricity at once, and pairs naturally with EV charging units.
carport.alt: Steel solar carport structure shading cars in a parking lot

f1.q: Who runs the permits and licensing?
f1.a: We do. Zoning status, EIA exemption or application, call letter and connection agreement — every project-development step is in scope.

f2.a: Rooftop systems typically run 4–8 weeks from survey to commissioning; unlicensed ground projects take 3–6 months depending on the permit calendar.

bess.metaDesc: Energy storage from LFP home batteries to container ESS: uninterrupted power, higher self-consumption, peak shaving.
bess.title: Energy Storage Systems
bess.intro: BESS stores electricity, generated or drawn from the grid, in batteries and gives it back the moment it's needed: it carries daytime solar into the evening, steps in during outages and puts you in charge of the bill.

aud1.title: Home
aud1.desc: Hybrid inverter + wall-mounted LFP battery: the house keeps running through outages, daytime production gets spent at night.

aud2.title: Commercial & Industrial
aud2.desc: Rack and container ESS: scalable capacity for peak shaving, demand management and grid services.

f1.q: Can storage be added to my existing PV system?
f1.a: Usually yes — by moving to a hybrid inverter or with an AC-coupled add-on unit. We measure the existing system during the survey and give a firm answer.

f2.q: How long do the batteries last?
f2.a: The LFP cells we use are 6,000+ cycle class — roughly 15 years at one charge-discharge a day. Capacity warranties are on the product cards.

flow.aria: Diagram showing energy flowing from solar panels through the inverter to the battery, the building and the grid

bess.scalesIntro: From a wall-mounted home battery to container-sized grid systems; your consumption profile sets the capacity.

home.title: Home
home.desc: A compact solution designed for a single household: wall-mounted LFP battery plus hybrid inverter.
home.b1: Stores surplus daytime production for the evening, raising self-consumption.
home.b2: During an outage the house switches to battery power automatically.
home.b3: On time-of-use tariffs it charges in cheap hours and spends in expensive ones.

ci.title: Commercial & Industrial
ci.desc: Scalable rack or cabinet systems for businesses, factories and commercial sites: the goal is lower cost and continuity.
ci.b1: Peak shaving: the battery steps in at peak consumption, cutting demand charges.
ci.b2: Demand management: spreading load over time for flat, lower costs.
ci.b3: Uninterrupted production: keeps critical lines from stopping.
ci.scale: Typical scale: 100 kWh to a few MWh

utility.title: Utility Scale
utility.desc: Container systems in the MW/MWh class connected directly to the grid, keeping the distribution network in balance.
utility.b1: Holds the grid steady with frequency and voltage regulation.
utility.b2: Smooths fluctuations in solar and wind output, storing and releasing on demand.
utility.b3: Energy arbitrage: stores cheap energy and feeds it back at peak demand.
utility.scale: Typical scale: a few MWh to hundreds of MWh

tech.p1: Most modern BESS units run on LFP (lithium iron phosphate) cells: high safety, a 6,000+ cycle life (about 15 years of daily use) and thermal stability.
tech.p2: The inverter handles DC-AC conversion; a smart battery and energy management system (BMS/EMS) governs charge-discharge balance, safety and grid compliance.

heatpump.metaTitle: Heat Pumps — Heating, Cooling, Hot Water and Pools
heatpump.metaDesc: Air-to-water heat pumps: one efficient system for underfloor heating, hot water and pool heating. Paired with PV, your heating runs on sunshine.
heatpump.title: Heat Pumps
heatpump.intro: Heating, cooling, hot water and underfloor circuits in one system: heat pumps turn each unit of electricity into 3–4 units of heat. With PV on your roof, your heating comes from the sun.

what.title: What is a heat pump?
what.p1: A heat pump is a high-efficiency climate system that heats, cools and produces hot water using the natural energy held in air, water or the ground. Instead of generating energy it transfers existing heat: high performance from low consumption, with lower carbon emissions.

how.title: How does it work?
how.p1: It moves heat energy from outdoors into the building; in summer it reverses direction and cools. Most of the energy it needs comes from nature, the rest from electricity. The result: high efficiency and low running costs. One system covers all three:

air.title: Air-Source Heat Pump
air.desc: Uses the energy in outdoor air for heating, cooling and hot water. The most popular choice for homes and commercial buildings.

water.title: Water-Source Heat Pump
water.desc: Draws its energy from groundwater, lakes or similar sources. Offers stable, high-efficiency operation.

geo.title: Ground-Source Heat Pump
geo.desc: Taps the steady natural temperature the ground holds year round. High efficiency and a long service life.

pool.title: Pool Heat Pump
pool.desc: Built to heat swimming-pool water economically and efficiently. Holds the water at the ideal temperature and stretches the season.

adv.a2: Covers heating, cooling and hot water in one system.
adv.a6: Long-lived and dependable in daily use.
adv.a8: Supports the use of renewable energy.

f1.q: Does a heat pump work efficiently in winter?
f1.a: Yes. Modern heat pumps are designed to run efficiently even at low outdoor temperatures. With the right capacity and engineering they heat effectively through winter.

f2.q: Do I still need natural gas?
f2.a: No. A heat pump can cover heating, cooling and hot water on its own, reducing or completely removing the dependence on gas.

f3.a: No. Because most of its energy comes from natural sources it uses electricity efficiently, with significant savings over conventional systems.

f4.a: Homes, villas, apartment buildings, hotels, offices, commercial and industrial facilities, and pool applications.

f5.a: Yes. Alongside heating and cooling it also covers domestic hot water.

f6.q: What does a pool heat pump do?
f6.a: It heats pool water economically using the energy in outdoor air; the swimming season stretches and energy costs drop.

f7.a: Yes. It cuts fossil-fuel use, lowers carbon emissions and draws most of its energy from renewable sources.

f8.a: The heat pump's consumption is covered by the sun: your heating cost comes from your roof, not your bill. We size both systems in a single project.

f1.q: Is my home's electrical infrastructure enough?

ac.lead: Ideal for daily, planned charging at home and work.

dc.title: DC Fast Charging
dc.lead: Minutes-scale charging on the road and in heavy use.

f2.a: On a 7.4 kW home unit a typical car fills overnight (6-8 hours). On DC fast charging the 20-80% window takes 20-40 minutes depending on the car.

f3.q: Does it work with my PV system?
f3.a: Yes. We set the car to charge on solar first; surplus production goes into the car instead of being sold to the grid.

f4.q: Can I bill users for charging at my business?
f4.a: Yes — OCPP-compliant units connect to operator platforms for kWh-based billing; we guide you through the licensing requirements.

With a team focused on energy engineering and more than 15 years of industry experience, we design, install and operate solar, energy storage, heat pump and EV charging solutions for homes and businesses, all from one hand. Our goal is clear: to turn the place you live into a harbor that powers itself.

We brought that experience under one roof: today, as MİNADA Enerji, we are an integrated energy partner delivering energy storage, heat pumps and EV charging alongside solar, all with the same team.

That is why we move through six transparent steps from survey to operation, so you know in advance what happens at every stage. Our offer is clear, our timelines are realistic, and our recommendations are tailored to your consumption.

Areas.title: One system, four scales
Areas.intro: From homes to industry, farms to public buildings: the four lines we build are the same everywhere. What changes is which one leads, and at what scale.
Areas.listIntro: Every setting has its own consumption curve and its own constraint, and the system design follows from that.

konut.title: Homes & Private
konut.desc: In villas, detached houses and gated communities the rooftop array, battery, heat pump and charger come together as one system.
konut.p1: Energy made in the day is carried into the evening, so less is drawn from the grid.
konut.p2: During an outage the house switches to the battery on its own.
konut.p3: The car charges overnight on energy the roof made that day.

ticari.title: Commercial & Industrial
ticari.desc: In factories, warehouses, industrial estates and hotels, large roofs and land become high-capacity plants.
ticari.p1: Production runs by day, so the consumption curve lines up with the sun.
ticari.p2: The battery steps in at peak hours, cutting demand charges and peak penalties.
ticari.p3: Charging for fleets and customers runs off the same system.

tarim.title: Agricultural Sites
tarim.desc: For irrigation, greenhouses, cold storage and livestock operations, energy stops being the largest line on the books.
tarim.p1: Irrigation pumps run in the hours the sun is strongest.
tarim.p2: With agri-PV the same land both generates and farms.
tarim.p3: Cold storage keeps running off the battery through an outage.

kamu.title: Public & Institutional
kamu.desc: For municipalities, schools, hospitals and public buildings the energy budget becomes predictable and critical loads are protected.
kamu.p1: The institution gets a predictable energy cost spread across years.
kamu.p2: Critical loads keep drawing from the battery the moment supply fails.
kamu.p3: Public charging points run on the institution's own generation.

Cookies.metaDesc: Which cookies the MİNADA Enerji website uses, what they do, and how to change your choice.
Cookies.title: Cookie Policy
Cookies.intro: This page explains which cookies minada.com.tr uses, what they do, and how you can change your decision.

s1.title: What is a cookie?
s1.p1: A cookie is a small text file your browser saves on your device when you visit a site. It lets the site remember you. Your browser's local storage does a similar job, and this policy covers both together.
s1.p2: Cookies are grouped by what they are for. Necessary ones exist so the site can work at all and need no consent. Nothing beyond those runs unless you allow it.

s2.title: The groups
s2.necessary: Necessary: things the site needs in order to function, such as your language preference and your cookie decision. Cannot be turned off.
s2.analytics: Analytics: measures in aggregate how much each page is read. Does not identify you as a person.
s2.marketing: Marketing: measures ad delivery and what visits from ads lead to.

s3.title: What is in use today
s3.intro: As of today this site keeps necessary records only. No third party analytics or advertising cookie is written, and no tracking request leaves the site. This table is updated whenever a new record is added.
s3.r1w: Remembers whether you want the site in Turkish or English.
s3.r2w: Stores the decision you make on this page so you are not asked again on every page. Kept in your browser's local storage and never sent to the server.

s4.title: Changing your decision
s4.p1: The "Cookie preferences" link at the foot of every page reopens the screen where you made your choice. You can withdraw consent there at any time.
s4.p2: You can also delete or block all cookies from your browser settings. If you block the necessary records, your language preference will not be remembered.

s5.title: Your rights and contact
s5.p1: For your rights regarding your personal data under Turkish law no. 6698 (KVKK), please get in touch with us.
